66:1: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Prophet, who forbade himself what God made lawful for him, seeking thereby to please his wives. Why do you forbid yourself what is lawful that God made lawful for you, seeking thereby to please your wives? Scholars differed about the lawful thing that God, the Most High, made lawful for His Messenger, but which he forbade himself in order to please his wives. Some of them said: It was his Coptic slave, Maria, whom he forbade himself by swearing that he would not approach her, seeking thereby the pleasure of his wife, Hafsa bint Umar, because she was jealous that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was alone with her on her day and in her room. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam told me, saying: Abu Ghassan told us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had intercourse with the mother of Ibrahim in the house of one of his wives. She said: O Messenger of God, in my house and on my bed! So he made her forbidden to him. She said: O Messenger of God, how can you make what is lawful forbidden to yourself? So he swore to her by God that he would not have intercourse with her. Then God Almighty revealed: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful to you, seeking to please your wives? Zayd said: So his saying, You are forbidden to me, is meaningless. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told me: Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Masruq said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade his slave girl and swore an oath against her, making what was permissible forbidden, and he said about the oath: God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths. Yunus bin Abdul-A’la told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, swore an oath and forbade it, so he was rebuked for forbidding it, and he was ordered to make expiation for the oath. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, he said to her: You are forbidden to me, by God I will not have intercourse with you. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? He said: Al-Sha’bi used to say: He forbade her to him, and he swore not to approach her, so he was rebuked for the prohibition, and the expiation came in the oath. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and Amir al-Sha’bi, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade his slave girl. Al-Sha’bi said: He swore an oath while forbidding her, so God rebuked him for forbidding her, and made expiation for the oath obligatory. Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? He said: A woman from the wives of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) found the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with his slave girl in her house, and she said: O Messenger of God, how did this happen, when I was the least important of them to you? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to her: Be quiet, do not mention this to anyone. She is forbidden to me if I ever approach her after this. She said: O Messenger of God, how can you forbid yourself what God has made lawful for you when you say, ‘She is forbidden to me forever?’ He said: By God, I will never approach her. Then God said, O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?... the verse, I have forgiven this for you, and your statement, by God, God has prescribed for you the expiation for your oaths, and God is your Protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a young girl, and he had intercourse with her. Hafsa saw him, and it was Aisha’s day, and they were both in a state of separation. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Keep it secret from me and do not mention to Aisha what you saw. So Hafsa mentioned it to Aisha, and Aisha became angry. She kept at the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he swore that he would never come near her again. Then God revealed this verse and commanded him to atone for his oath and go to his slave girl. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Aamer, regarding the statement of God, O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? regarding a slave girl whom he came to, and Hafsa saw him, so he said: She is forbidden to me, so keep it secret and do not tell anyone about it. So she mentioned that. Others said: Rather, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade his slave girl, so God Almighty made his forbidding her equivalent to an oath, and He required for her the same expiation as He required for an oath if its owner broke it. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths, God commanded the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers, if they forbade something that God had made permissible for them, to expiate their oaths by feeding ten poor people or clothing them, or freeing a slave, and that does not come under the heading of divorce. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? until His statement, And He is the Knowing, the Wise. He said: Hafsah and Aisha loved each other and they were both wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Hafsah went to her father and talked with him, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for his slave girl, and she stayed with him in Hafsah’s house. The day came when Aisha was to come, so Hafsah returned and found them in her house. She waited for her to come out and became extremely jealous. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought out his slave girl, and Hafsah entered and said, I saw who was with you, and by God, you have upset me. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, By God, I will please you, for I am confiding in you a secret, so keep it. She said, What is it? He said, I bear witness that this slave girl of mine is forbidden to me, in order to please you. Hafsah and Aisha used to swear On the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so Hafsa went to Aisha and whispered to her: Be happy, for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, has forbidden his girl to him. When she told the secret of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, God Almighty revealed it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then God revealed to His Messenger when they conspired against him: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? until His saying: And He is the Knowing, the Wise. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Hisham al-Dastawa’i told us, he said: He wrote to Yahya, narrating on the authority of Ya’la ibn Hakim, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, that Ibn Abbas used to say: Indeed, in the Messenger of God you have a good example to follow (al-Ahzab 33:21), meaning that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade his slave girl, so God, the Most High, said: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? until His saying: God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths, so he expiated his oath, so the forbidden became an oath. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, who said: Abu Uthman told us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered Hafsa’s house, and she was not there. His young lady came to him, and he threw a curtain over her. Hafsa came and sat at the door until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished. She said: By God, it has made me sad. I had intercourse with her in my house, or something like that. He said: And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade her from having intercourse with her in my house, or something like that. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?... the verse. He said: He forbade his Coptic girl, the mother of his son Ibrahim, whose name was Maria, on the day of Hafsah, and he confided that to her, so Aisha found out about it, and they used to support each other against the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So God made lawful for him what he had forbidden for himself, so he was commanded to expiate for his oath, and he was rebuked for that, so He said, God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths, and God is your Protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise. Qatada said: Al-Hasan used to say that he forbade her, so God made it lawful for him to expiate for an oath. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade her, meaning his slave girl, and she was Yemeni. “Saeed bin Yahya told us: My father told us: Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I said to Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: Who are the two women? He said: Aisha and Hafsa. The conversation began with the matter of Umm Ibrahim Al-Qibtiyya. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had intercourse with her in Hafsa’s house on her day. Hafsa found him and said: O son of God, you have done something to me that you have never done to any of your husbands on my day, in my turn, and on my bed. He said: Are you not satisfied that I forbid her and not approach her? She said: Yes. So he forbade her and said: Do not mention that to anyone. So I mentioned it to Aisha, and God Almighty made it clear to him, and God revealed: ‘O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? ’... all the verses. It has reached us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, atoned for his oath and had intercourse with his slave girl.” Others said: It was a drink he drank, he liked it. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad bin Al-Haad, who said: This verse was revealed regarding alcohol: O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, seeking to please your wives? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Qatn Al-Baghdadi Amr Ibn Al-Haitham told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qais Ibn Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Shaddad, similarly. He said: Abu Qatan told us, he said: Yazid bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said: It was revealed about alcohol. The correct thing to say about this is: What the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade himself was something that God had made permissible for him. It is possible that it was his female slave, or it is possible that it was a drink, or it is possible that it was something else. However, whichever it was, it was forbidding something that was permissible for him. So God rebuked him for forbidding himself what he had made permissible for himself, and explained to him that his oath was permissible in an oath that he had sworn with while forbidding what he had forbidden himself. If someone were to say: What is your proof that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) swore while forbidding what he had forbidden? You know the statement of those who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did nothing in that regard other than forbidding, and that forbidding is an oath. It is said: The proof for that is clear, which is that it is not conceivable in an Arabic or foreign language that the statement of one to one’s slave girl, or to food or drink, This is forbidden to me, is an oath. So if that is not punishable, then it is known that an oath is not the statement of God, who says to something that is permissible for him: It is forbidden to me. If that is the case, then what we have said is correct, and what contradicts it is invalid. And further, it is possible that the prohibition of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was what he had forbidden himself from the permissible things that God, the Exalted, mentioned, had made permissible for him with an oath. So his statement, Why did you forbid what God had made permissible, means: Why did you swear about something that God had made permissible that you would not approach it, and forbid it to yourself with an oath. We said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade that, and swore an oath while forbidding it, as: Al-Hasan bin Qaz’ah told us: Muslima bin Alqamah told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, swore an oath and forbade himself from having intercourse with her. He ordered expiation for the oath, and it was said to him regarding the forbidding of intercourse: Why did you forbid yourself what God has made lawful for you? And His statement: And God is Forgiving and Merciful, God Almighty says: And God is Forgiving, O Muhammad, of the sins of those of His servants who repent from their sins, and He has forgiven you for forbidding yourself what God has made lawful for you. He is too Merciful to punish His servants for the sins they have repented of after repentance.
66:2: God Almighty says: God Almighty has made clear to you the way to dissolve your oaths, and He alone is for you, O people, and God is your protector who supports you with His victory, O believers, and He is the All-Knowing of your interests, the All-Wise in His management of you and directing you in what He knows best.
66:3: God Almighty says, “And when the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, confided in one of his wives,” and according to Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Zayd ibn Aslam and his son Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, al-Sha’bi, and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, it was Hafsa. We have already mentioned the narration on this matter. His saying: A recent hadith. The hadith that he confided in her, according to these people, is his saying to whomever he confided in of his wives, that his girl was forbidden, or what he had forbidden himself from what God, the Most High, had made permissible for him, and his swearing on that and his saying, Do not mention that to anyone. And His statement: So when she informed him of it, God Almighty says: So when she informed her companion of the hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had confided in her, and God made it manifest to him, meaning: God made His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, manifest, because she had informed her companion of that. His saying: He knew some of it and ignored some of it. The reciters differed in their recitation of that. The majority of reciters in the regions, except for Al-Kisa’i, recited it as he knew with a shaddah on the ra, meaning: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew some of that hadith from Hafsa and informed her of it. Al-Kisa’i mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami and Qatada that they read it as (‘arfa) with a light ra’, meaning: He knew to Hafsa some of that action that she had done by revealing his secret, and he had kept it a secret from her, meaning that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry with her and punished her for it, like the saying of one who wronged him, I will surely know for you, O so-and-so, what you did, meaning: I will punish you for it. They said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, punished her for that action of hers by divorcing her. The first of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the correct reading of the one who read it as Arafat Ba’dhu with a shaddah on the ra, meaning: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew Hafsa, meaning what God revealed to him of her hadith, her companion, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on this. And his saying: And he turned away from some means: And he left out telling her about some of it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives, his saying to her: Do not mention it. “But when she informed him of it and God made it manifest to him, he recognized part of it and ignored part.” And he was generous, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: So when he informed her of it, meaning when Hafsa informed the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what God had revealed to him of her divulging the secret of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Aisha, She said, ‘Who informed you of this?’ He says: Hafsa said to the Messenger of God: Who informed you of this report and told you about it? “He said, ‘The All-Knowing, All-Aware informed me.’” God Almighty says: Muhammad, the Prophet of God, said to Hafsa: The All-Knowing informed me of it, the One who knows the secrets of His servants and the innermost thoughts of their hearts, the All-Aware of their affairs, from whom nothing is hidden. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, So when he informed her of it, she said, ‘Who informed you of this?’ and she had no doubt that her companion had informed her, He said, ‘The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me.’
66:4: God Almighty says: If you both repent to God, O women, your hearts have inclined toward loving what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, hated, which was his avoiding his concubine and forbidding her to himself, or forbidding what was lawful for him from what he forbade himself because of Hafsa. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, If you both repent to God, then your hearts have indeed deviated, meaning: Your hearts have deviated, meaning: Your hearts have sinned. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Muhammad bin Talha told us, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: We used to think that his statement, For your hearts have indeed deviated, was something insignificant, until I heard Ibn Masoud recite: If you both repent to God, then your hearts have indeed deviated. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: For your hearts have turned away means your hearts have turned away. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Qatada: Your hearts have become inclined. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, For your hearts have turned away, meaning: they have deviated. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: Your hearts have become corrupted. He said: Your hearts have deviated. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: God Almighty said: If you both repent to God, your hearts have already become corrupted. He said: It pleased them that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would avoid his slave girl, and that was in accordance with them. Your hearts have already become corrupted until what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked pleased them. And His statement, And if they both conspire against him, God Almighty says to the one to whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, confided his hadith, and the one to whom she divulged his hadith, and they are Aisha and Hafsa, may God be pleased with them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la narrated: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Thawr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I was always keen to ask Umar about the two women from the wives of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about whom God, the Most High, said: If you both repent to God, your hearts have indeed become inclined. So Umar performed Hajj, and I performed Hajj with him. When we were on the way, Umar turned aside, and I turned aside with him by bringing a water skin. Then he came to me, and I poured water over his hand and performed ablution. Then I said: O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two women from the wives of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about whom God said: If you both repent to God, your hearts have indeed become inclined. Umar said: How strange you are, Ibn Abbas. Al-Zuhri said: By God, he disliked what he asked him and did not conceal it. He said: They are Hafsah and Aishah. Then he began to narrate the hadith, saying: We, the Quraysh, used to dominate women, but when we came to Madinah… Then he mentioned the hadith in full. Yunus told me: Ibn Ashhab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Nadr, on the authority of Ali ibn Husayn, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, asked him about the two women who conspired against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Aisha and Hafsa. Yunus narrated: Ibn Wahb narrated: Sufyan narrated: Yahya ibn Sa`id narrated: Ubayd ibn Hunayn narrated that he heard Ibn Abbas say: I spent a year wanting to ask Umar ibn al-Khattab about the two women who had conspired against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but I could not find a place to ask him, until he went out for Hajj. I accompanied him until he reached Marr al-Dhahran. He went to relieve himself and said: Bring me a water skin. When he had relieved himself and returned, I brought him the water skin to pour it over him. I saw a place and said: O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two women who conspired against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? I had not finished speaking when he said: Aisha and Hafsa may God be pleased with them both. Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Umar bin Yunus told us: Ikrimah bin Ammar told us: Samak Abu Zamil told us: Abdullah bin Abbas told us: Umar bin Al-Khattab told us: When the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) withdrew from his wives, I went to him and I saw anger on his face. I said: O Messenger of God, what is so difficult for you regarding women? If you divorced them, then God and His angels, Gabriel and Michael, and I and Abu Bakr are with you. I rarely spoke and praised God except that I hoped that God would confirm my words. Then this verse was revealed, the verse of choice: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you. “And if they both back him up against him - then indeed, God is his Protector, and so is Gabriel and the righteous believers.”... The verse. Aisha, the daughter of Abu Bakr, and Hafsa used to back each other up against the rest of the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And if they both back up one another against him, meaning: to disobey the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and harm him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, Ibn Abbas said to Umar: O Commander of the Faithful, I want to ask you about something and I fear you. He said: Do not fear me. He said: Who are the two who conspired against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Aisha and Hafsa. And his saying: Then God is his Guardian and Gabriel and the righteous believers means: Then God is his Guardian and Supporter, and the righteous believers: and the best of the believers are also his Guardian and Supporter. It was said: What is meant by the righteous believers in this place are: Abu Bakr and Omar, may God be pleased with them. Who said that? Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Azdi told me: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Abdul-Wahhab, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and the righteous believers, he said: Abu Bakr and Umar. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement, and the righteous believers, he said: The best of the believers are Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq and Umar. Ishaq bin Israel told us: Al-Fadl bin Musa Al-Sinani from a village in Marv called Sinan told us on the authority of Ubaid bin Sulayman, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim say regarding His statement, and the righteous believers, he said: Abu Bakr and Umar. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, and the righteous believers, that he said: The best of the believers. Others said: What is meant by the righteous believers are the prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, and the righteous believers, he said: They are the prophets. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, and the righteous believers, he said: They are the prophets. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: And the righteous believers means the prophets. The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is that his statement, and the righteous believers, even if it is in one wording, has the meaning of all, and it is in the same sense as his statement, Indeed, mankind is in loss (Al-‘Asr: 2). So, even if the word human is in one wording, it has the meaning of all, and it is similar to a man saying, Do not recite except to the reciter of the Qur’an. It is said, the reciter of the Qur’an. Even if it is in one wording, its meaning is the plural, because he has given permission to every reciter of the Qur’an to recite it, whether it is one or a group. His statement, And the angels after that will be a support, means: The angels, along with Gabriel and the righteous believers, will be helpers for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, against those who harmed him, meaning those who offended him. The support in this instance is in one word with the meaning of a group, and if it had been presented in the wording of all, it would have been said: And the angels after that will be a support. Ibn Zayd used to say about this: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And if they both back up one another against him - then indeed, God is his Protector, and so is Gabriel and the righteous believers, he said: And He began with the righteous believers here before the angels, and said, And the angels after that are supporters.
66:5: God Almighty says: Perhaps if the Lord of Muhammad divorces you, O wives of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, He will replace you with wives better than you. It was said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a warning from God to his wives who gathered against him in jealousy. Who said that? Abu Kurayb and Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told us: Hisham told us: Hamid al-Tawil told us, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: The wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered around him out of jealousy, so I said to them: Perhaps if he divorces you, his Lord will replace you with wives better than you. So it was revealed thus. Yaqub narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of Umar, he said: I was informed that some of our mothers, the Mothers of the Believers, were harsh with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and that they were harming him. So I asked them, woman by woman, to admonish them and forbid them from harming the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and I would say: If you stay overnight, God will replace you with wives better than you, until I came. I thought that he had spoken about Zaynab, so she said: O son of Al-Khattab, is there not in the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) enough to admonish his wives so that you should admonish them? So I held back, and God revealed: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you all, will give him in exchange wives better than you. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: I heard something about the Mothers of the Believers, so I asked them, saying: Either you refrain from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or God will replace him with wives better than you, until I came upon one of the Mothers of the Believers, and she said: O Umar, is there not in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, enough to admonish his wives so that you admonish them? So I refrained, and God revealed: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, submissive and believing... the verse. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement that He replaces it. Some of the reciters of Mecca, Medina, and Basra recited it with a shaddah on the dal yubidluhu awwajan from the word tabadulu, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it yubidluhu with a light dal from the word ibdal. The correct thing to say is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. His saying, Muslims, means: Submissive to God in obedience. Believers, meaning those who believe in God and His Messenger. And his saying obedient means: obedient to God. As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God’s statement obedient, he said: obedient. Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, obedient, he said, obedient. His saying, repentant, means: returning to what God loves from them in terms of obedience to Him, and away from what He hates from them. Worshipping, means: humbled before God in obedience to Him. And his saying travelers means: fasting. The interpreters differed about the meaning of his statement, travelers. Some of them said: It means: fasting. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, traveling women, he said: fasting women. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Wandering women, he said: Fasting women. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: The wandering ones are the fasting ones. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Wandering, meaning: Fasting. Others said: The female tourists are the female immigrants. Who said that? Ishaq bin Abi Israel told us: Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad Al-Darawardi told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, who said: The female travelers are the emigrants. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Travelers, he said: Migrants. There is no travel in the Qur’an or in the nation of Muhammad except migration, and it is what God said, Travelers (al-Tawbah 9:112). We have already explained the correct statement regarding the meaning of the travelers previously, with evidence, and we mentioned the statements of those who differed about it, and we disliked repeating it. Some Arab scholars used to say: We believe that the fasting person is called a traveler because the traveler does not have any provisions with him, but rather eats wherever he finds food, so it is as if he took from that. His saying, those who have not had intercourse or divorced.
66:6: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, Protect yourselves meaning: Teach one another what the one you know will say about the Fire, and ward it off from him if he acts in obedience to God, and act in obedience to God. His saying, And your families, a Fire, means: Teach your families to do acts of obedience to God that will protect them from the Fire. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement, Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, he said: Teach them, educate them. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ali: Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire. He said: Discipline them, teach them. Al-Husayn bin Yazid Al-Tahhan told me: Saeed bin Khathim told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Khalid Al-Dhabi, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ali, similarly. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire, meaning: Do what God commands, avoid what God commands, and command your families to remember God, and God will save you from the Fire. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire, he said: Fear God, and advise your families to fear God. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones. He said: He protects them by ordering them to obey God and forbidding them from disobeying Him, and by carrying out God’s command over them, ordering them to do it and helping them to do it. So if you see God being disobeyed, he deters them from it and warns them against it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire, he said: Command them to obey God and forbid them from disobeying Him. His saying, Its fuel is people, means: Its firewood that is lit on this fire is the children of Adam and sulfur stones. And His statement, Over it are angels, stern and severe, meaning: Over this fire are angels from the angels of God, stern and severe towards the people of the fire. They do not disobey God in what He commands them, meaning: They do not disobey God in what He commands them. They do what they are commanded, meaning: They adhere to what their Lord commands them to do.
66:7: God Almighty says, informing us of what He will say on the Day of Resurrection to those who denied His Oneness in this world: O you who disbelieve in God, “Make no excuses today. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.” He says: It will be said to them: You are only being rewarded today, and that is the Day of Resurrection, and you will be given the reward for the deeds you used to do in this world, so do not seek excuses for them.
66:8: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God, repent to God. He says: Return from your sins to obeying God and to what pleases Him with you. A sincere repentance. He says: A return in which you will never return. And in a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of His saying, sincerely, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samalik, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, who said: Umar was asked about sincere repentance. He said: Sincere repentance is when a man repents from a bad deed, then never returns to it again. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, on the authority of Umar, who said: Sincere repentance is that you repent from the sin and then do not return to it, or do not want to return to it. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, who said: I heard Al-Nu`man bin Bashir giving a sermon. He said: I heard Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: O you who have believed, repent to God with sincere repentance. He said: He commits a sin and then does not go back on it. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, who said: I asked Umar about his statement, Repent to God with sincere repentance. He said: It is the servant who repents from sin and then never returns to it again. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, who said: I heard Umar bin Al-Khattab say: Sincere repentance is to repent from the sin and not return to it. Ibn Hamid told us about it again. He said: Omar told me with this chain of transmission. He said: Sincere repentance is when someone commits a sin and does not want to return to it. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah: Sincere repentance. He said: He repents and then does not return to it. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Sincere repentance is when a man commits a sin and then does not return to it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, O you who have believed, repent to God with sincere repentance, that its doer not return to the sin from which he repents, and it is said: His repentance is that he does not return to the sin he abandoned. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told me, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, sincere repentance, he said: They seek forgiveness and then do not return to it. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement, sincere repentance, he said: Sincere repentance means that you turn away from the sin and then never return to it again. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: O you who have believed, repent to God with sincere repentance. He said: It is the sincere and sincere repentance. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding the statement of God, Repent to God with sincere repentance, he said: Sincere, honest repentance, he knows that it is true regret for his sin and love to return to His obedience, so this is honesty. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of reciters of the regions, except for Asim, recited it as Nasuhan with a fat-ha on the nun, as a description of repentance and its attribute. It was reported from Asim that he recited it as Nasuhan with a damma on the nun, meaning the source from their saying: So-and-so advised so-and-so sincerely. The more correct of the two readings is the one that reads it with the opening of the letter nun as an adjective for repentance, due to the consensus of the authorities on that. And His statement, It may be that your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds, meaning: It may be that your Lord, O believers, will erase the misdeeds of your past deeds, and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, meaning: And admit you to gardens beneath whose trees rivers flow, on the Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who believed with him, their light will proceed before them, meaning: Their light will proceed in front of them, and on their right, meaning: And on their right is their record. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, On the Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believe with him... until His statement, and with their right hands, they will take their book in which is good tidings, They will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us,' God, the Most High, says, informing us of what the believers will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:They will say, Our Lord, perfect for us our light, they will ask their Lord to keep their light for them and not extinguish it until they have crossed the bridge, and that will be when the hypocrites, men and women, will say to those who believe, Wait for us so that we may borrow from your light. (al-Hadid 57:13) And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Our Lord, perfect for us our light, he said: The statement of the believers when the light of the hypocrites is extinguished. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: There is no one who will not be given light on the Day of Resurrection. It will be given to the believer and the hypocrite, and the light of the hypocrite will be extinguished. The believer will fear that his light will be extinguished, and that is what His saying, Our Lord, perfect for us our light. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Yazid ibn Shajarah, who said: He used to remind us and cry, and his actions would confirm his words. He would say: O people, you are written with God, the Almighty, by your names, your features, your gatherings, your private conversations, and your private conversations. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, here is your light. O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, there is no light for you. His saying, And forgive us, means: And cover our sins for us, and do not disgrace us with them by punishing us for them. Indeed, You are over all things competent, means: You are capable of completing our light for us, and forgiving our sins, and other things.
66:9: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Prophet, fight the disbelievers with the sword and the hypocrites with threats and the tongue. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, he said: God commanded His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and to be harsh with the hypocrites with the prescribed punishments. And be harsh with them means: be severe with them for the sake of God. And their refuge is Hell means: their abode is Hell, and their destination to which they will go is the fire of Hell. And evil is the destination means: and evil is the place to which they will go is Hell.
66:10: God Almighty says: God’s example for those who disbelieve among mankind and all creation is the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our servants, Noah and Lot, and they had sexual intercourse with them. It was mentioned that Noah’s wife betrayed her husband because she was an unbeliever, and she used to tell al-Nas 114:He is crazy. And that Lot’s wife betrayed him because Lot used to please the guest, and she used to guide him. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Sulayman bin Qais, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and they betrayed them, he said: Noah’s wife used to say to the people, He is crazy, and Lot’s wife used to guide the guest. Muhammad bin Mansur al-Tusi told us: Ismail bin Umar told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Sulayman bin Qays, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say about this verse: As for Noah’s wife, she used to say that he was crazy, and as for Lot’s wife’s betrayal, she used to point out Lot. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Amir al-Hamadhani, on the authority of al-Dahhak: They were under two of Our righteous servants. He said: No woman of a prophet ever transgressed against him. And betrayed them. He said: They betrayed them in religion. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding His statement, “God presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them.” He said: Their betrayal was that they were not of the same religion. Noah’s wife was aware of Noah’s secret, so if someone believed with Noah, she would inform the tyrants of Noah’s people about him, and that was her command. As for Lot’s wife, if someone hosted Lot, she would inform the people of the city about him who did evil. But they did not avail them at all against God. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Amr Ibn Abi Sa`id, that he heard `Ikrimah say about this verse, And they betrayed them. He said: In religion. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them. He said: Their betrayal was that they were polytheists. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: They betrayed them. He said: They were disobedient to the religion of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and disbelieved in God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah al-Bajali, he said: I asked Saeed ibn Jubayr: What was the betrayal of Lot’s wife and Noah’s wife? He said: As for Lot’s wife, she used to guide guests, but as for Noah’s wife, I have no knowledge of her. His statement, And they did not avail them at all against God, means: Noah and Lot did not avail their wives at all against God when He punished them for their betrayal of their husbands, and it did not benefit them that their wives were prophets. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “God sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot”... the verse, these two were the wives of the Prophet of God, when they disobeyed their Lord, their wives could not avail them against God at all. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: “God sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot”... the verse. He said: God says: The righteousness of these two did not benefit those two at all, and the wife of Pharaoh was not harmed by Pharaoh’s disbelief. And His saying, And it will be said, ‘Enter the Fire with those who enter.’ God will say to them on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Enter, O two women, the fire of Hell with those who enter it.
66:11: God Almighty says: And God has set forth an example for those who believe in God and believe in His Oneness: the wife of Pharaoh, who believed in God and believed in His Oneness, and believed in His Messenger Moses, while she was married to an enemy of God’s enemies, a disbeliever. Her husband’s disbelief did not harm her, as she believed in God. And it was God’s decree for His creation that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and that every soul shall have what it has earned. When she said, My Lord, build for me, near You, a house in Paradise, God answered her and built for her a house in Paradise. Ismail bin Hafs Al-Ayli told me: Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman, who said: Pharaoh’s wife was being tortured by the sun, and when he turned away from her, the angels would shade her with their wings, and she would see her house in Paradise. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told us: Asbat bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, who said: Salman said: She was the wife of Pharaoh, and he mentioned something similar. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawa’i: al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza told us: Pharaoh’s wife used to ask who had won. They would say: Moses and Aaron have won. She would say: I believe in the Lord of Moses and Aaron. So Pharaoh sent to her and said: “Look for the biggest rock you can find. If she insists on what she says, then throw it on her. But if she retracts her statement, then she is his wife.” When they came to her, she raised her eyes to the sky and saw her house in the sky. She continued with what she said, and God took her soul away, and the rock was thrown on a body that had no soul. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, “And God presents an example to those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh.” He was the most rebellious of the people on earth against God, and the most distant from God. By God, her husband’s disbelief did not harm his wife when she obeyed her Lord, so that you may know that God is a just judge, and He does not hold His servant accountable except for his sin. And His saying: And save me from Pharaoh. And you say: And save me from the punishment of Pharaoh, and from doing his deeds, and that is his disbelief in God. And His saying, And save me from the wrongdoing people, means: And save me and rescue me from the actions of the people who disbelieve in You, and from their punishment.
66:12: God Almighty says: “And God presents an example to those who believe: Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity.” He says: The one who guarded her garment from Gabriel, peace be upon him. And every tear or crack in the armor is called a chastity, and likewise every crack and fissure in a wall, or the opening in a ceiling, is a chastity. And His saying, Then We breathed into him of Our spirit, means: We breathed into him into the pocket of her garment, which is her vagina, of Our spirit from Gabriel, which is the spirit. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then We breathed into him of Our spirit. “Then We breathed into her bosom of Our spirit.” And she believed in the words of her Lord. He says: She believed in Jesus, who is the Word of God. And His books. He means the Torah and the Gospel. And she was among the obedient. He says: She was among the obedient people. As Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, of the obedient is of the obedient.
